questions.stem: A histogram bar has width $5$ and frequency density $3.2$. What is the frequency for that class?
Why do histograms have no gaps between the bars?

options.text: To make them look different from bar charts
Because the data is continuous, so the classes are connected
Because the class widths are all equal
To save space on the page

questions.explanation: Histograms represent continuous data where each class interval follows immediately from the previous one with no gaps. The bars touch to show this continuity.
